text:
ben (Customer SRE): Hey team, since 03:20 UTC our Private control plane mTLS connections from our VPC are intermittently failing. We upgraded an inline DLP/egress appliance earlier and saw failures spike after that. Symptoms: short TLS handshake, then `alert handshake_failure (40)` on client side.

sara (Support): Sorry you're hitting this, can you paste a short tcpdump/openssl test? Any changes to client cert rotation or MTU?

ben (Customer SRE): Repro steps below. Happens 7/10 times.
1) curl --key client.key --cert client.crt --tlsv1.3 https://controlplane.private.redwood.internal/ping -v
2) sometimes returns `error:1401E0E5:SSL routines:tls_construct_client_hello:no protocols available` or quickly `alert handshake_failure`

Example openssl s_client output when it fails:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect controlplane.private.redwood.internal:443 -cert client.crt -key client.key -tls1_3 -msg
<< TLS 1.3, Handshake [length 0032]
<< 01 00 00 2e 03 03 ... ClientHello
<< TLS 1.3, Alert [length 0002]
<< 02 28
---
SSL alert number 40\n---
```
\nraj (NetOps): Are we sure the SNI/client_hello reaches the server intact? Our inline appliance does TLS record reassembly and sometimes rewrites application-level headers for inspection. Could be splitting the ClientHello across TCP segments.

ben (Customer SRE): I captured a pcap. Notice how the TLS record is split and the final fragment is rewritten by the appliance (it injects a tiny TCP RST/retrans pattern). Packet shows `TLS record fragment: length 16` then `length 0` effectively truncating client_hello.

sara (Support): That matches past cases where middleboxes resegment TLS and the server-side TLS stack rejects the incomplete record. Two asks: 1) can you temporarily bypass the appliance for Redwood control-plane IPs (egress allowlist) and confirm? 2) if bypass not possible, collect server logs for `TLS record` / `bad record mac` / `alert 40`.

ben (Customer SRE): Bypassing the appliance for the control plane IPs makes the problem go away immediately. With bypass enabled, all handshakes succeed.

eng-oncall: Escalating to runtime team — looks like our control plane was strict about record boundaries on the mTLS endpoint. We already tolerate fragmentation but this appliance manipulates/rewrites bytes mid-record which breaks MAC verification for TLS 1.3. Sending the captured pcap to eng channel.

raj (NetOps): For short-term mitigation we've added a firewall rule to SNAT the traffic through a separate egress path that doesn't touch the DLP appliance. Long-term we'll ask vendor for a config that preserves TLS record boundaries and disable opportunistic reassembly.

sara (Support): Action items:
- Customer: keep bypass for control-plane IPs (tested).
- NetOps: file vendor ticket with pcap + reproduce steps (include MSS/MTU and TCP options).
- Eng: confirm if server can tolerate this pattern or add clearer error messaging (log: `mtls: client hello truncated by egress rewrite`).

deploy-bot: [deploy] rolled patch 2026-03-10T04:12 -> controlplane-mtls: added more descriptive handshake failure logs (mtls: incoming record corrupted)

eng-oncall: Just pushed a log patch, please re-run repro and attach the server logs. If we see `incoming record corrupted` we can close with vendor config. If not, we'll request a small protocol workaround.

ben (Customer SRE): Confirmed after bypass everything is green. Will keep bypass in place while vendor fixes their inline reassembly. Thanks all :thumbsup:

sara (Support): Marking this as customer-resolved (temporary bypass). We'll follow up on vendor ticket and eng fix.

ben (Customer SRE): FYI, vendor response: they consider it TLS-inspection normal behavior but will provide a setting to "preserve record fragmentation". We'll ask for a firmware release.

sara (Support): Thanks — please paste vendor ticket link when available and we'll keep the support thread open until vendor patch shipped and tested.
